body: Pocket Card Jockey is Game Freak's Nintendo 3DS combination of horse racing and a solitaire card game. A jockey's performance at the cards affects the progress of the horse, turning a familiar tabletop routine into part of a sporting contest. Between rounds the player chooses a position on the track, then builds toward the final stretch. The two activities continually feed one another. Clearing a line of cards is satisfying in itself, but its immediate consequence is that the horse and rider become better prepared for what is happening above.

The card game follows the golf-solitaire rule of selecting a card one rank above or below the current one. A good sequence clears the field while preserving cards in the deck, improving the unity between horse and jockey. Excess unity can become energy for the race. The touchscreen is also used to position the horse with the surrounding field in mind. These decisions give the cards a setting beyond the table: their result creates an opportunity, but the player still has to use that opportunity sensibly on the track.

Horses develop during a period of racing before reaching maturity, after which repeated losses eventually lead to retirement. Retired horses can breed, allowing a successful career to influence the next generation. The longer structure gives an unlucky race a place inside a wider attempt to build a capable stable. Pocket Card Jockey keeps those sporting ambitions approachable through its small, repeated card rounds. Each race offers another immediate puzzle, while the horse's growing history provides a reason to care about where the next run will leave it.
